title: CTO Conversation Guide: Differentiators and Pricing Scenarios
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:

This page is a concise, sales-facing playbook designed for conversations with CTOs, VP Engineering, and platform leads evaluating inference infrastructure. It combines high-level positioning, explicit differentiators compared to common alternatives, three pragmatic pricing scenarios with assumptions, brief objection responses, a short anonymized case study, and a compact security FAQ to use during technical calls. Use this as a single-sheet reference before and during technical discovery.

One-line positioning for CTOs:

Redwood Inference: predictable, high-throughput LLM serving that lets platform teams govern cost, latency, and deployment mode (hosted / dedicated / private) without building an inference stack from scratch.

Audience and use-cases:
- CTOs evaluating inference for product features (search, summarization, copilots)
- Platform teams deciding between cloud-managed endpoints and self-hosted runtimes
- Procurement / security stakeholders needing an operational and compliance story

Key differentiators (talking points):
1) Deployment parity: single API + tooling across Hosted API, Dedicated GPU pools, and Private VPC/on-prem installs — reduces integration complexity and supports multi-environment rollouts.
2) Production economics controls: explicit knobs for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles with measurable cost deltas.
3) Smart routing & graceful fallbacks: policy-driven routing by latency/cost/region and automatic fallback to compatible model variants during capacity constraints.
4) Observability & attribution: per-token cost breakdowns, per-model latency histograms, and token-level tracing for debugging regressions.
5) Kernel & runtime optimizations: architecture-aware kernel selection and KV cache management tuned for sustained throughput.
6) Enterprise-grade operations: SLA-backed Dedicated, audit logs, KMS integrations for Private deployments, and formal runbooks for upgrades and rollbacks.

Competitive snapshot (concise grid for quick reference):
Note: competitors are anonymized categories to keep this doc evergreen.

| Dimension | Managed LLM Platforms (Large Cloud) | Open-source Self-host / Inference Stack | Redwood Inference (us) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Time-to-value | Fast (managed endpoints) | Slow (internal ops) | Fast (hosted) + predictable for Dedicated/Private |
| Cost transparency | Low (complex bills) | High variability | High (token/unit economics + tooling) |
| Deployment options | Limited (cloud only) | Flexible but high maintenance | Multi-mode: hosted, dedicated, private |
| Reliability & fallbacks | Region-dependent | Operator-managed | Built-in fallback policies, canary rollouts |
| Observability | Varies | Requires custom tooling | Native dashboards: per-route, per-token, eval regressions |
| Enterprise controls | Varies | Full control but heavy lift | Enterprise features + support for Private/KMS/auditing |

Pricing scenarios (examples to use in discovery; show order-of-magnitude economics). Assumptions: baseline LLM (2B–13B range), token pricing converted to monthly, includes compute + networking + platform fees for Hosted; Dedicated shown as committed monthly for equivalent throughput; Private shown as license + support amortized monthly. These are illustrative—use deal desk for final numbers.

Scenario A — Early product pilot (low usage)
- Monthly request volume: 25M tokens
- Model: moderate (7B) on Hosted API
- Typical latency target: 200–300ms
- Economics estimate: Hosted plan: $1,800–$2,800 / month
- Recommended approach: Hosted API with evaluation credits, SLO of 200–500ms, track cache hit rates

Scenario B — Growth / production feature (steady mid usage)
- Monthly request volume: 500M tokens
- Model: 13B (mixed accuracy/latency)
- Typical latency target: 100–200ms
- Economics estimate: Dedicated reserved capacity: $12k–$25k / month (depends on commit and burst policy)
- Recommended approach: Jump to Dedicated with autoscale policy and prefix-caching enabled; include cost profiling in Redwood Console

Scenario C — Regulated or data-sensitive (enterprise)
- Monthly request volume: 1B+ tokens
- Model: 13B–70B (quantized variants for cost)
- Typical latency target: 50–200ms (region-dependent)
- Economics estimate: Private deployment: license + infra (example amortized figure) $40k–$120k / month (depends on on-prem hardware)
- Recommended approach: Private deployment with KMS, audit logging, and SRE runbook; pilot with a Dedicated fall-through for burst capacity

How to present pricing in a discovery call (recommended script):
1) Confirm token volume ranges and peak concurrency.
2) Ask about latency SLOs and data residency needs.
3) Offer a straightforward Hosted projection for pilots, a Dedicated estimate with commit tiers for steady-state, and a Private architecture ballpark if compliance requires it.
4) Emphasize unit economics levers (batching, cache, quantization) that can reduce cost by 20–60% depending on workload.

Sample pitch deck outline (6–8 slides; use as starter):
1) Executive summary (one slide): problem, Redwood as the solution, primary ROI metric (cost per 1M tokens or latency improvement)
2) How teams break inference complexity: deployment parity + operational controls
3) Performance & reliability story (benchmarks + SLOs)
4) Economics: pricing scenarios and cost reduction levers
5) Security & compliance (audit logs, KMS, network isolation)
6) Migration path & timeline (pilot -> Dedicated -> Private)
7) An anonymized case study with measured outcomes
8) Next steps & ask (POC criteria, decision owners, procurement path)

Objection handling cheatsheet (short responses):
- "We can self-host and save money."
  Response: "You can, but the surface area includes kernel tuning, batching, KV cache management, upgrade rollback processes, and model-variant routing. Many teams end up spending 3–6x engineering time beyond initial expectations. Redwood purpose-built tooling buys that time back while preserving cost controls."
- "I need strict data residency and key control."
  Response: "We provide Private deployments with KMS/HSM integrations and an isolated control plane. We also support dedicated cloud tenancy for stricter network controls."
- "How do we avoid quality regressions after model changes?"
  Response: "We tie quality monitoring to prompt sets and eval baselines, with regression alerts prior to rollout and canary A/B policies that automatically fallback."

Short anonymized customer case study (engineer-facing):
- Customer: Large B2B search product (GA 2025)
- Challenge: Unpredictable unit cost and frequent latency spikes during peak queries
- Solution: Pilot on Hosted API; migrated high-volume traffic to Dedicated with prefix caching and model quantization for bulk inference. Implemented per-route dashboards and automated fallback policies.
- Results (90 days): 45% reduction in average per-token cost, 60% reduction in 95th percentile latency, and zero production incidents related to inference during the migration window.

Security FAQ (short, shareable answers for prospects):
Q1: Where does data go when using Hosted API?
A1: For Hosted API, request payloads are processed in the region selected at configuration and retained per retention policy. We offer options to disable logging of raw inputs and token-level artifacts for sensitive workloads.

Q2: Can we manage encryption keys?
A2: Yes. Private deployments support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. For Dedicated customers, KMS integration is available for stored artifacts and audit logs.

Q3: What audit capabilities exist?
A3: Token-level audit trails, model version auditing, access logs, and admin activity logs are available and can be exported to SIEM solutions.

Q4: How are upgrades and CVEs handled in Private deployments?
A4: We publish upgrade schedules and security advisories. We ship hotfixes for critical CVEs and provide a documented upgrade and rollback runbook. For Private, we coordinate upgrade windows with the customer’s SRE.

Q5: Do you support network isolation / VPC peering?
A5: Yes. Private deployments support VPC-only access and optional on-prem installation; Dedicated supports private subnets and restricted egress configurations.

Q6: What compliance frameworks do you support?
A6: Redwood maintains documentation and processes to support SOC 2 readiness, and we assist enterprise customers with architecture patterns for ISO/GDPR compliance. Formal attestation depends on the deployment model.

Q7: How do you prevent model leakage or exfiltration?
A7: Controls include request/response masking, retention controls, KMS for stored artifacts, and network egress restrictions; we also recommend application-level filtering for sensitive prompts.

Q8: Can we run an air-gapped deployment?
A8: Yes—our on-prem Private packaging supports air-gapped installs with customer-managed model assets and telemetry collectors controlled locally.

Practical call checklist (what to capture during the technical discovery):
- Primary decision owners and procurement timelines
- Current monthly token volumes (p50, p90, p99) and concurrency peaks
- Latency SLOs and acceptable 95th percentile targets
- Data residency, key management, and compliance needs
- Existing inference architecture and pain points (ops time, incidents, costs)
- Willingness to pilot (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and target success metrics

Appendix: quick configuration table (example knobs and recommended defaults)

| Knob | Description | Starter default | Impact on cost/latency |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Batch size | Number of requests batched for the same model | 4–16 requests | Increases throughput, may add tail latency |
| Prefix / KV cache | Cache warm KV for conversational workloads | Enabled for sessions > 3 turns | Reduces per-token compute by 10–40% |
| Quantization profile | Lower-precision model variant | 4-bit/8-bit where compatible | Lowers compute cost 20–60%, may affect accuracy |
| Autoscale policy | Burst capacity and commit thresholds | Steady baseline + 2x burst | Controls Dedicated cost and availability |
